code_hints: If URL contains a fragment (e.g., #product-information-panel), remove it and reload before scraping.
Before PLP detection, click OneTrust consent if present using #onetrust-accept-btn-handler.
If no PLP tiles are found but CTA buttons exist on the landing page, click one of cta_to_plp to reach the PLP.
Wait for article[data-test='product-tile'] or a[data-test='product-tile-link']; scroll a few times to trigger lazy loading.
If current URL locale is en-jp, normalize to en-int and retry (avoid region-specific interstitials).
On PDP, if visible price selectors fail, parse JSON-LD (script[type='application/ld+json']) for price/name as a fallback.
Avoid treating editorial anchors like #product-information-panel as PLP; prefer navigating to a dedicated listing via CTA or normalized URL.
rationale: We landed on a marketing/legal-like landing page with a fragment and a double-locale path (/en-jp/en-int/), which likely triggers region/interstitial content. Normalizing to en-int and stripping fragments avoids the trap. Moncler commonly uses OneTrust, so adding consent handling prevents blocking overlays. The landing page often has CTAs (Shop the collection/Shop now) that lead to the real PLP; adding CTA selectors provides a safe click-through path. Product tiles on Moncler frequently use data-test product-tile link patterns; adding those wait-for and link selectors enables extraction once on the PLP. PDP price/title fallbacks include JSON-LD to increase robustness.
